# NOTES ON THE TEXT (compact reference)

Two books, separated below under their headings.

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The B. O. W. C.: A Book For Boys" by Prof. James De Mille (1871, Lee and Shepard, Boston; author of "The Dodge Club"; dedicated "To Willie")

**Setting:** Grand Pré School (Acadian/Nova Scotia area; Dr. Porter head master), Minas Basin, Bay of Fundy. Spring vacation, May.

**Characters:**
- Bart Darner: fair, curly golden hair, merry; inventive; ran away twice from school; leader of B.O.W.C.; carries pistol and leather cup; father a St. John merchant.
- Bruce Rawdon (elder) and Arthur Rawdon (younger): brawny, Roman features, dark curling hair, twins-like; brothers.
- Tom Crawford: tall, slight. Phil Kennedy: small, slight.
- Solomon: old African cook, "Perpetual Grand Panjandrum"; "Venerable Warden" role played by Bart; uses dialect.
- Mr. Simmons (mathematics, minerals); Mr. Long (English, hard-driving, energetic, later emotional).
- Captain Corbet: schooner Antelope owner, babbling, obsessed with infant "babby"; wife Mrs. Corbet; mate Wade (wife "Gipson").
- Pat (Michael Murphy): Irish, sky-blue coat, silk hat; Johnny Blue (Peter Fraser); Bogud (David Digg, geology); Muckle (George McLeod); Jiggins (Jacob Wiggins); Billymack (William MacNamara); Sammy Bam Ram (George Henderson).
- Captain Pratt: owner of Pratt's Cove; Mrs. Pratt: home medicine chest.
- Dennis O'Rafferty and wife Molly: on Five Islands; son Michael died 1845 aged 15.
- Bogud, Sammy, Johnny Blue, Pat, etc.

**B.O.W.C.** = Brethren of the Order of the White Cross. Officers: Most Venerable Patriarch, Venerable Scribe, Right Worshipful Commander, Grand Scholastic, Venerable Warden. Costume: red shirts with white cross, belts, plumed felt hats. Black flag with grinning skull-like bald face, initials. Phrenological bust. Solomon made "Perpetual Grand Panjandrum."

**Plot sequence:**
1. Opening meeting in Rawdons' rooms; Solomon's turkeys (10), chickens (20), ginger beer; Bart reveals costumes and black flag.
2. Procession to woods with Solomon in cart; camp by pond and brook; Bart's fog-horn, pistol. "Gaspereaugians" rivalry.
3. Dr. Porter offers schooner cruise; Antelope (Capt. Corbet) chartered; boys stripped/ballast from Mr. Brown's garden wall; Corbet absent tending baby; boys sleep aboard; Corbet's fence theft; black flag raised.
4. Blomidon (name said to be "Blow me down"); Captain Kidd songs; seasickness; Five Islands; Pinnacle Island; Bruce climbs cliff for gull's nest, root gives way; Bart and Arthur haul him up; Mr. Long's emotion.
5. Anchor, fog, Bruce rows boat with Arthur/Bruce; Bruce collapses ("I'm dying"); boat lost in fog. Mr. Long blows fog-horn all night; Corbet's anchor drift.
6. Boys wash ashore on separate island; cook lobster in hot stones ("Micmac way"); tire of lobster; Phil's signal flag (red shirt on tree); O'Rafferty's house.
7. O'Rafferty rescues, gives hatchet with initials; Phil's omelette; ship rescued at Pratt's Cove.
8. Pratt's Cove: boys eat turkeys, Pat & Johnny Blue cook duck and pig; Pat's "stones" (minerals) thrown into water; Jiggins, Muckle ate clams raw; Mrs. Pratt's medicines ("clams poison in months without R").
9. Schooner drifts; boys run aground; shovel-mouth shark fight; sculpin; retrieval of schooner; Mr. Long rescues boys from water/mud; Pat's discarded minerals lost; Mr. Long's "Antelope" drifts back; Corbet's compass theory ("the apostle Paul had a compass"); boys sing; final mud-flat crossing at Grand Pré; Solomon's "Wenebble" greeting; feast.

**Notable quotes:** "Blood!" / "Thunder!" (gesture). "Yes, sah, mos' wossifle." "Blow me down." Corbet: "babby," "parygolic," "Bo-rax."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "A Witch of the Hills" by Florence Warden (London, Richard Bentley & Son, 1888, 2 vols; author of "The House on the Marsh")

**Narrator:** Henry Lyttleton "Harry" Maude, nicknamed "Handsome Harry," aged 39 (later ~36 and ~38 in notes); inherited £8,000/yr at 23. Disfigured by accidental gun shot (right face, eyebrow gone, hand lost two finger joints). Lives at Larkhall, Deeside near Ballater, Scotland; shooting-box near Loch Muick; forest and Craigendarroch hill.

**Friends:** Lord Edgar Normanton (Helen's brother; later married; "the elephant"); Fabian Scott (actor, artist; Scottish; fiancé then husband of Babiole); William/Richard Fussell (jolly, City man, separated wife); Maurice Browne (realist author, pallid, pink-rimmed eyes); Lady Helen Normanton (fiancée; daughter of Marquis of Castleford; "fairy face"; Helen of portrait).

**Babiole Ellmer** (Babiole = "little witch", blue eyes, gold-brown curly hair; age 8 at first meeting; "Mr. Maude"): daughter of Mrs. Ellmer (actress, thin, sharp, mother, "Miss Bailey") and Mr. Ellmer (drunk, painter, violent, "Bob" actor-manager's colleague). Mrs. Ellmer's stage names: Diana Vernon, Helen Macgregor.

**Major events in order:**
- Vol I Ch. I–II: Maude's engagement to Lady Helen; quarrel with Edgar at Norfolk shooting party (Sir Wilfrid Speke host); accidental shot to face/right shoulder; Edgar nurses him. Maude decides to leave England.
- Ch. III: Maude's letter releasing Helen; her reply ("MY DEAREST HARRY"); Helen faints at his disfigured face; he has false eyebrow, moustache, hair.
- Ch. IV–V: Aberdeen, Saturday night, Fabian Scott at the Strand stage door; Ellmer swaggering; Babiole's apple/kiss game. Five years wandering; Ferguson (John Ferguson, Scottish manservant, sabre scar; mother Janet). Maude finds Mrs. Ellmer & Babiole performing at Aberdeen; offers cottage at Larkhall.
- Ch. VI–VII: Cottage furnished secretly; Ferguson and monkey To-to (brown, chained, jealous of collie Ta-ta); Maude overhears Mrs. Ellmer call him "hideous wicked face"; chimney smoke; dinner party; Babiole sees portraits of "Helen" (two pictures).
- Ch. VIII: Babiole, age 14, climbs Craigendarroch; "love one knows but once"; Mrs. Ellmer's flirtations.
- Ch. IX: Friends' visit August 15; Fabian flirts with Babiole ("we're going to be married"); Fabian kisses her goodbye.
- Ch. X–XI: Lessons begin (French, Latin); Maude goes to Norway; returns; friends' disputes; Babiole reads novels (Ivanhoe, Armadale, Clarissa); Ellmer appears; Maude teaches her.
- Ch. XII–XIII: Ellmer visits, demands Maude marry Babiole; Maude proposes "engagement" as guardian; Babiole accepts; Ellmer calls him to account; kiss in front of Ellmer.
- Vol II Ch. XIV–XV: Friends' visit (Edgar engaged to Miss Farington); Fabian flirts with Babiole; Maude asks Fabian to leave; Braemar coach trip; Babiole cries at Fabian's departure.
- Ch. XVI–XVIII: Mrs. Ellmer "pushes" match; Babiole's love-sickness; Maude sends her to London? No: Maude goes to London; Fabian proposes; Babiole marries Fabian at Newcastle (wedding; Maude gives her away; Mrs. Ellmer keeps Ta-ta). Maude abroad four years.
- Ch. XIX–XX: Fabian & Babiole in London; Fabian's affair with Countess (Lady of Kensington Palace Gardens); Babiole's unhappy marriage; Maude declares love; Miss Lucy Farington (Liverpool solicitor's daughter, philanthropist, plans for school/cottage); engagement, later broken off (Lucy's letter: "returns letters").
- Ch. XXI–XXIII: Babiole returns to Larkhall (after Fabian's arrival planned); Babiole's sleepwalking; Fabian's misdirected letter (appointment in Edinburgh, Royal Hotel); Ellmer escapes asylum with gun, kills Fabian in snow on forest road by mistake for Maude (Jock the gillie with lantern; "Mistress Scott bid me gang wi' ye").
- Ch. XXIV–XXVI: Ellmer dies; Babiole's relief ("Then it was not you!"); Maude declares feelings; Babiole leaves for France/Algeria companion job; letter ends with April spring, Babiole's letter "Babiole wants me; God bless her!"

**Key quoted phrases:** "Poor little witch!"; "Handsome Harry"; "Babiole wants me; God bless her!"; "Ta-ta, old girl"; "Auld Robin Gray"; "The Stirrup Cup"; "Did you see what was played?"
